name: Discovery Completion Strategy
description: Configuration for determining when Discovery has enough understanding without relying on fixed question counts or scripted completion.

completionSignals.name: Sufficient Confidence
completionSignals.description: Core observations have confidence levels appropriate to their importance and evidence.

completionSignals.name: Evidence Density
completionSignals.description: Important insights are supported by enough participant statements, examples, or recurring themes.

completionSignals.name: Coverage Quality
completionSignals.description: Relevant discovery domains have been explored to useful depth, with thin areas clearly identified.

completionSignals.name: Understanding Depth
completionSignals.description: The agent can describe meaningful patterns, uncertainty, and unresolved tensions without overclaiming.

completionSignals.name: Participant Confirmation
completionSignals.description: Important identity, meaning, values, motivations, and narrative themes have been offered back for participant confirmation, correction, or refinement.

completionSignals.name: Participant Readiness
completionSignals.description: The participant appears ready to pause, close, or receive a summary of what has been understood.

avoid: Completing because every schema field has been touched shallowly.
Completing when conclusions are mostly unsupported.
Completing by treating unconfirmed observations as final identity claims.
prefer: Confidence appropriate to the claims being made.
Participant ownership of the stopping point.
Clear separation between observed themes, participant-confirmed themes, and open questions.
